title: In an abstract group, the inverse of the inverse is the original element
statement: For any group record G (an abstract carrier, binary op, identity e, inverse, associativity, two-sided identity and inverse laws) and element a of G's carrier, inv (inv a) = a.

formal.statement: theorem Alg.neg_neg : ((x0 : Alg.Group) -> ((x1 : Alg.Group.carrier x0) -> Eq.{1} (Alg.Group.carrier x0) (Alg.Group.inv x0 (Alg.Group.inv x0 x1)) x1))

evidence.supports: Alg.neg_neg admits through the trusted kernel gate as a DIRECT INSTANTIATION of Alg.groupInvUnique at (x := inv a, b := inv (inv a), c := a), h1 := invL(inv a), h2 := invL a -- no new proof engineering. Instantiated CONCRETELY at Int.addGroup (a := 3) with the type checked to reduce to Eq 3 3, and SYMBOLICALLY at Rat.addGroup closed over a free a.
evidence.checker_command: out=$(cargo test -p axeyum-lean-kernel --lib -- neg_neg_applies_concretely_at_int_and_symbolically_at_rat --nocapture --test-threads=1 2>&1) && test "$(printf "%s\n" "$out"| grep -cE 'test result: ok\. 1 passed; 0 failed')" -ge 1

evidence.supports: Alg.neg_neg instantiated at Rat.addGroup has the SAME TYPE as the hand-proved Rat.neg_neg -- a genuine retirement candidate. Int.addGroup has NO retirement counterpart: int_prelude/gcd.rs's `neg_neg` is a private Rust proof-term HELPER (`pub(super) fn neg_neg`), never declared as a kernel-visible theorem, so Alg.neg_neg instantiated at Int.addGroup is a NEW top-level fact for Int, not a retirement.
evidence.checker_command: out=$(cargo test -p axeyum-lean-kernel --lib -- retirement_rat_neg_neg --nocapture --test-threads=1 2>&1) && test "$(printf "%s\n" "$out"| grep -cE 'test result: ok\. 1 passed; 0 failed')" -ge 1

notes: Retires Rat.neg_neg (same type). Does not retire anything at Int: int_prelude has no declared Int.neg_neg theorem, only a private helper -- so this is the first place Int's double-negation fact becomes a kernel-checkable NAME, reachable via Alg.neg_neg Int.addGroup, rather than a new one.
